analysis:
This PR only changes CI plumbing and documentation: cache restore/save logic, sparse and partial checkouts, a changelog entry and docs/developer/build.md. It does not touch provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, key custody or the prefix cache. The retained T-041 concerns the runtime SSD prefix cache, not CI caches, so it does not apply. I found no change to the threat-model assets or trust boundaries.

I examined the visible ci.yml head lines 541-1199, the docs-impact.yml patch, and the docs and changelog text. The `.git` cache is restored in every run, and `SAVE_CACHES` (ci.yml line 17-ish per the patch) restricts saving to push events on master or dev. Pull requests, including untrusted code, therefore cannot poison caches that later privileged or trusted runs restore. That is a net hardening. Two further hardening points: `persist-credentials: false` keeps the job token out of the cached `.git/config`, and a `git fsck --connectivity-only` plus HEAD verification step discards a damaged restored `.git` (e.g. ci.yml lines 678-684). All cache actions are pinned to commit SHAs.

The docs-impact job's `blob:none` filter and sparse checkout exclude only `docs/reports/**/*.gz` and `landing/public/**/*.mp4`. This reduces fetch size and does not weaken the check, assuming the claimed property that no script reads those files, which I cannot verify from the supplied evidence.

Residual unverified items outside the supplied units: ci.yml lines 1-540 and the `.github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml` composite action (SwiftPM, Swift build and Metal cache keying). These were only visible through the patch excerpt and docs. They affect CI integrity only and not the runtime threat model. No findings.
